newsitem.title: SWEDEN: NORDBANKEN SAYS EYEING MARKET OPENINGS.
newsitem.headline: NORDBANKEN SAYS EYEING MARKET OPENINGS.

text.p: Swedish state-controlled bank Nordbanken said on Wednesday it will guard its market position and utilise opportunities that could come up in connection with the restructuring of the country's bank sector.

"In the ongoing restructuring of the Swedish finanical market Nordbanken must guard its position and make use of the possibilities that can be created," Nordbanken's chief executive Hans Dalborg said in the bank's annual report.

"Our position must be to seek combinations that can increase the bank's competitiveness, create additional value for customers and value for shareholders at the same time as Nordbanken's strength and development is taken care of."
The Swedish banking sector has experienced a recent shake out.
In February, rivals Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced they would merge and competitor Handelsbanken finalised its acquisition of mortgage bank Stadshypotek .

Merger talks between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken, which is 59 percent owned by the state, collapsed in early February with no clear reason given although it was believed to be over management differences.
Dalborg said Nordbanken will keep its focus on the Swedish market but added that distribution should be Nordic.
"Nordbanken is a Swedish bank and will remain so," Dalborg said.
"But the Nordic region is for many a common market and distribution forms or services functioning in Sweden should also be used in the other Nordic countries."
Growth in the Baltic region creates future possibilities for Swedish banks, he said.
"Nordbanken will take care of the opportunities this (Baltic region growth) creates," Dalborg said.

"Sweden's European Union membership, the creation of the European economic and monetary union (EMU) and the business sector's increased internationalisation demand Swedish banks that can be equal with the best European banks."
